slide_1.title_shape: Large-Scale AI Transformation Narrative Across Multiple Business Units
slide_1.first_textbox: During a twelve-month transformation program, five departments introduced separate AI workflows for forecasting, quality monitoring, customer support, and logistics optimization. Each rollout required cross-functional governance meetings, regional compliance checks, model validation signoffs, and detailed rollback planning before production release.
slide_1.second_textbox: Program leadership then consolidated metrics from all workstreams into one operating cadence, including incident rates, drift alerts, false positive investigations, staffing impacts, and finance-controlled cost baselines. This exposed misaligned ownership boundaries and forced teams to redesign escalation protocols and reporting responsibilities.
slide_1.third_textbox: Multi-region rollout dependencies created repeated schedule slippage when approval gates were not synchronized across legal, platform, and operations stakeholders.
slide_1.fourth_textbox: Incident response handoffs became inconsistent because communication templates differed by department and on-call coverage did not include shared fallback ownership.
slide_1.fifth_textbox: Executive review required weekly remediation snapshots
